name: Home Addition vs ADU: Which Makes More Sense?

mainEntity.name: How do custom home additions differ from ADUs in Los Angeles County?
mainEntity.text: How do custom home additions differ from ADUs in Los Angeles County?

acceptedAnswer.text: Custom additions and ADUs solve different space problems, even though both add square footage. A home addition extends the main house for more living area, such as a larger family room, bedroom, or expanded primary suite. An ADU is designed as a secondary residence, so it must function more independently and often requires its own kitchen, bathroom, and living areas. That changes the design approach, budget, and approval process. In Los Angeles County, the decision often comes down to whether the homeowner wants more space for the family or a separate unit for rental income, multigenerational living, or guest use. A contractor can help compare site constraints, utility tie-ins, and return on investment before the project is defined too narrowly.
acceptedAnswer.description: A home addition expands the primary residence, while an ADU creates a separate secondary living unit with independent function. Additions usually integrate into the main home’s layout, while ADUs often require separate kitchen and bathroom planning, privacy considerations, and different utility arrangements. The design, permit strategy, and long-term use case are not the same.
